name: kissat
why: A top-tier SAT solver; watching clause learning crack hard Boolean puzzles is a real door into solver internals.

brief.what_it_is: Kissat is a SAT solver: a program that takes a Boolean formula and reports whether some assignment of true/false to its variables satisfies it, usually in CNF form, and returns a satisfying assignment or an unsatisfiability answer. The README describes it as a "keep it simple and clean bare metal SAT solver" written in C. It is a port of CaDiCaL back to C, with new data structures and different scheduling of inprocessing. The README does not document input or output formats or command-line usage beyond the build step.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a simpler, cleaner C solver built from CaDiCaL's ideas, with better data structures, better scheduling of inprocessing, and optimized algorithms. It was entered in the SAT Competition 2024 as the sc2024 version. The release notes say that version dominated the competition and won three gold medals in the main track categories (SAT, UNSAT, SAT+UNSAT).
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. The release notes name several techniques: clausal congruence closure (congruence.c), bounded variable addition (factor.c), fast variable elimination during preprocessing (fastel.c), vivification of clauses, local search for initial phases, and probing and elimination on a scheduled interval. These come from the NEWS file, not the README.

commands_seen.context: Configures, builds, and runs the test suite in a build directory. The README gives this as the way to build from source.

From the 3.1.0 release notes: removes the macOS quarantine attribute from the unzipped Apple arm64 binary when Safari downloads trigger a launch error. The release notes say building from source is the alternative if you do not want to strip quarantine.

brief.install_notes: Build from source with ./configure && make test, which builds in a build directory. Prebuilt binaries are attached to each major GitHub release. On macOS, a binary downloaded through Safari may need the quarantine attribute removed (see commands_seen) or be fetched with wget. The README mentions no runtime, accounts, or configuration beyond that.
brief.standout: It is a deliberate re-implementation of CaDiCaL in plain C with a stated goal of simplicity, and its 2024 competition entry won several gold medals. The name is a pun: kissat is Finnish for cats, and the README points this out.
brief.status: Maintained. The latest GitHub release is 4.0.4, dated 16 Oct on the releases page (the year is not shown in the fetched text). Before it came 4.0.3 (28 Jun), 4.0.2 (24 Jan), and 4.0.1 (12 Sep), with 4.0.0 (27 Jul) as the competition version. The NEWS file is up to date with 4.0.4 at the top. I did not check the most recent commit date.
brief.caveats: The README gives no usage guide, so the command-line interface and input format need reading from the source or other docs; I did not fetch those. The only build path described is ./configure and make, with no alternative package manager. The license badge shows MIT. The 3.1.0 Apple binary had a Gatekeeper quarantine issue. The scout note says watching clause learning crack hard puzzles is a good way into solver internals, but the README does not mention that and I have not verified it.

judge.reason: Kissat is an obscure, competition-dominating SAT solver whose preprocessing and clause-learning machinery make Boolean satisfiability a hands-on rabbit hole.

entry.title: Kissat
entry.tldr: A competition-winning SAT solver in plain C that decides whether a Boolean formula can be satisfied, and a door into how modern solvers work.
entry.deeper_look:
Kissat takes a Boolean formula, usually in CNF form, and reports whether some assignment of true and false to its variables makes it true. If one exists, it returns it. If none does, it says the formula is unsatisfiable. The README calls it a "keep it simple and clean bare metal SAT solver written in C."

It is a port of CaDiCaL back to C, with new data structures and a different schedule for inprocessing, which is simplifying and rewriting the clause set while the search is running. The release notes name techniques such as clausal congruence closure, bounded variable addition, fast variable elimination, clause vivification, and local search to pick initial phases. The 2024 version, sc2024, won three gold medals in the SAT Competition 2024 main track.

The idea underneath is that a huge class of problems can be written as true/false constraints and handed to one general engine. Scheduling, hardware verification, and puzzles all reduce to SAT. Kissat is a place to see how far that engine has been pushed. The name is a pun: kissat is Finnish for cats.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the command-line options, which is the quickest way to learn the interface since the README gives no usage guide.

entry.whats_unique: It is a deliberate rewrite of CaDiCaL in plain C, aimed at simplicity, and its 2024 competition version took several gold medals.
entry.caveats: The README documents only the build step, so input format and options have to be learned from --help, the source, or other docs; you also need your own CNF files to feed it.
